_why: Same-account remote conversation tools address a pair of hostId and threadId. Local aliases must retain existing behavior while an explicit foreign host must never fall through to a same-id local conversation. Remote reads must retain the destination host in their nested thread header, and wait snapshots, cursors, failures, and wake identities must remain distinct across hosts. Receiver delivery is idempotent for one caller-provided return address and requestId within the authenticated destination account, including retries after the original caller disconnects. The return address is routing metadata, not authorization; every reply must independently resolve and authorize its destination under the replying account. These vectors pin observable routing and snapshot behavior; the companion tests connect two real ThreadToolsService instances through a bounded fake relay. Unconfirmed admission and confirmed removal preserve stable messageId through both relay ends instead of becoming generic errors that invite unsafe resends. Collection hints retain public host/thread identities, including same-id chats on different computers. Unconfirmed or removed messages do not receive a successful collection hint.
